Hi everyone! Our AI4Math team at BICMR@PKU, led by Prof. Bin Dong, is excited to introduce Archon—an agentic system built for research-level formalization in Lean 4.

We recently tested Archon on the FirstProof challenge with promising results: the system successfully formalized Problem 6 fully autonomously and completed Problem 4 with only a single informal hint from a human expert. By integrating Claude Opus 4.6 with our mathematical MCP tools like LeanSearch, Archon effectively bridges the gap between human-level informal proofs and rigorous Lean implementation.

We believe this demonstrates a path toward making formalization a high-efficiency, interactive process where AI handles the syntactic heavy lifting. You can read the full announcement and explore our formalization results here.
Our Github repo: https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-FirstProof-Results

We would love to hear your thoughts and welcome any discussion on the results!
Is Archon itself available anywhere for testing?

Przemek Chojecki said:

Is Archon itself available anywhere for testing?

Currently, Archon still requires some additional engineering work before it can be easily deployed on other machines, and the present version is also too costly for most individual use cases. Unfortunately, this means it is not yet suitable for public testing.

That said, we are actively running Archon on a number of selected on-going formalization repositories to better understand how it can support the community, while continuously refining its skills and overall system design (we’ll share more details about this in the upcoming blog post). We do plan to make a more mature version publicly available in the coming months—though users will need to provide their own API keys.
Would love to test it once available!

We've published a technical blog post diving into Archon's architecture, our dual-agent workflow, and the key lessons we learned from formalizing FirstProof Problems 4 and 6. Check it out here: https://frenzymath.com/blog/archon-firstproof/

Guoxiong Gao said:

We've published a technical blog post diving into Archon's architecture, our dual-agent workflow, and the key lessons we learned from formalizing FirstProof Problems 4 and 6. Check it out here: https://frenzymath.com/blog/archon-firstproof/

Congrats! Can you say precisely how long Archon was running for each Problem 4 and Problem 6. What would be interesting is also a precise info like it run for 5 hours, then there was human interventation, then another 4 hours, etc. This would be helpful to understand it better.

Thanks for the question! We have mentioned the overall runtime in the news: about 50 hours for Problem 4 and 30 hours for Problem 6.

Regarding the human intervention you asked about, for Problem 4 the only human hint was given roughly 8 hours before completion. After that, Archon spent about 2 hours resolving this final remaining sorry. During its subsequent self-check, Archon realized that what it had proved was only a weaker version of the target statement, since it had not accounted for the case where p and q have multiple roots. It then spent another 4 hours repairing that part and completing the full proof. The final 2 hours were used to clean up the development and do some light refactoring.
This topic was moved here from #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Archon: Auto-Formalization of FirstProof Problems 4 & 6 by Kim Morrison.

The Archon system is now open-sourced at https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon. It is designed to be easily customizable, allowing users to adapt skills and prompts to their own projects. We also provide guidance for integrating Archon with orchestrators (e.g., OpenClaw), enabling more powerful usage. We would greatly appreciate any feedback.
Have you thought about trying on autoformalization benchmarks like the FormalQualBench? Can it be used with other models like Leanstral?

I would love to see this run against Lecture 1 from https://math.mit.edu/classes/18.785/2025/lectures.html (possibly more of them too!)

edit: I've posted separately explaining why I'd like to see people try this one

Jason Rute said:

Have you thought about trying on autoformalization benchmarks like the FormalQualBench? Can it be used with other models like Leanstral?

We haven’t tested Archon on FormalQualBench yet, but since it is fully open-sourced, you’re welcome to try it out. If we were to run an official evaluation, we would likely make some small prompt adjustments and enhance the informal agent. The current version of Archon is primarily designed to collaborate with mathematicians on project-level formalization, rather than to generate a standalone formal proof for a single statement without informal guidance. In this context, encouraging the Plan Agent to first obtain a solid informal proof could potentially improve performance, though this is less critical for project-based workflows where a given blueprint is already available.

As for Leanstral, I would not expect it to outperform Sonnet given the reported lower single-pass scores. That said, it is still worth trying, especially since it is open-source and inexpensive. In practice, the actual cost can differ quite a bit from API pricing—for example, running an agent continuously under a $200 Claude Max plan may correspond to a much higher amount of API usage (roughly $6000-$10000 by my estimate, though this may not be precise). For scientific comparison we look at API prices, but as users we care more about actual cost; in this sense, Claude Code (even the $20 plan with Sonnet) still seems like a strong option to me.

Hi everyone! Our AI4Math team at BICMR@PKU, led by Prof. Bin Dong, previously announced Archon, an agentic system for research-level formalization in Lean 4, after it completed two problems from FirstProof.
Archon's Github repository has now reached 122 stars. Thank you for all the interest and feedback, it feels like the right moment to share an update, as Archon has been updated to v0.2.0 with a substantial redesign that makes the system more reliable and easier to use.
You may also be interested to know that Archon was recently used in the automated resolution of an open conjecture in commutative algebra, see our blog post for details.
Here is a brief summary:

  • Installation now requires only one single command line

  • Despite more features, getting started is easier, the interface guides the user

  • Archon can run on a Claude Code subscription, or via Anthropic / DeepSeek / Kimi / OpenRouter API keys

  • Archon now interacts directly with leanblueprint, can retrieve and read papers and textbooks to reduce hallucination, and is supervised by fresh-context subagents that verify and auto-correct the agent's output

  • Users have more control: agents, subagents, and skills can be customized; hints can be added to help/correct Archon ; can freeze some signatures that shouldn't be touched by Archon ; and archon discuss opens a direct interactive session with Archon's context

All in all, Archon makes fewer mistakes, makes wiser plans, is more resilient to difficulty, and is more honest when to criticizing its own work. 
Archon keeps improving thanks to your feedback, it is very welcome! We are continuing to run Archon on formalization projects and will share more results soon.

Hi everyone! There were no answers to the previous message, but I hope people who would like to be aware of such updates are able to find this thread to read it :hug: . It is important however to announce  :sparkles: v0.3.0 :sparkles: because Anthropic changed claude -p's billing method today. Therefore, we made it possible to use Codex instead of Claude Code, and also added some alternative backends to keep using Claude Code within the max/pro plan, allowing everyone to use Archon almost exactly like before, with the same billing.

Despite this, we have also integrated Archon with a DAG structure, which it can communicate with. This allows the system to ground its work deeply in mathematical references, guiding its proof strategy with a deterministic graph instead of the LLM's internal representation of it.
